subject.title: [BUG] memory index --force CLI writes incompatible meta providerKey, breaks runtime memory_search

question: Should Memory Core auto-repair or rebuild stale CLI/runtime providerKey and scope identity metadata, or keep the current fail-closed behavior until the user runs an explicit repair?
rationale: The code can be changed mechanically, but the product choice is whether provider/model/scope drift is considered recoverable stale metadata or a safety boundary that must stay paused to avoid mixing embeddings from different providers or settings.

options.title: Sponsor narrow recovery
options.body: Add a tested, narrow Doctor/runtime recovery for known stale CLI-written identity states while continuing to fail closed on real provider, dimension, endpoint, or scope changes.

options.title: Keep fail-closed
options.body: Document the pause behavior as intentional and require users to run explicit rebuild or Doctor repair when identity metadata differs.

options.title: Wait for related PRs
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/91660 and the open memory identity issues as the first landing path before deciding broader recovery policy.

recommendation.title: Sponsor narrow recovery
recommendation.body: Add a tested, narrow Doctor/runtime recovery for known stale CLI-written identity states while continuing to fail closed on real provider, dimension, endpoint, or scope changes.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans memory-core identity safety, provider routing, and recovery policy, and this history points most strongly to steipete as the current area owner.
